observations: A dark red silhouette of a bulky rounded figure occupies the center-left of a flat yellow field, leaning back with an oversized rounded head shape tilted far to the right.
Yellow outline strokes trace internal divisions—torso, limbs, a dangling rounded foot—visible against the dark red fill, so figure and ground colors swap roles along those edges.
Thin forked lines rise from the top of the figure into open yellow space, unattached to the solid mass below; a small jagged mark sits on the large rounded head at right.
reading: The figure leans back hard, weight dropping through the lower body while the oversized head swings wide to the right. Thin forked lines at the top float free of the solid mass below. The two-color scheme keeps the image flat and high-contrast, and the yellow outline strokes inside the silhouette suggest a body under strain rather than at rest.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #262 and nnxyz nnotb #264. All three use a two-color figure-on-ground structure, but #263 strips the field to near-silence compared to the dense layering visible in #262.

connections.reason: Both #263 and #264 place a single solid-fill figure on a plain ground using two colors, and both figures lean with limbs extended away from the body's center mass.
#114 shares the same yellow ground and a dark silhouetted figure with thin radiating lines extending outward, offering a direct formal parallel to the forked lines above #263's figure.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the thin forked lines at the top connect to—or fail to connect to—the solid mass of the figure below?
ambiguities: The jagged mark on the large rounded head shape may be a face detail or an incidental mark; image resolution does not resolve this clearly.
Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align for this work, but gaps exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so adjacency does not confirm sequential making.
